purpose: Detect repeated same-cycle shared transport failures across the Defence health estate while preserving raw failures and keeping target-specific failures outside shared-transport recurrence qualification.

states.stable: No qualifying shared-transport cycles exist in the lookback window.
states.watch: Qualifying shared-transport cycles exist but remain below the recurrence threshold.
states.recurrent: The recurrence threshold has been met or exceeded.

qualification: Probe results are grouped by scheduled request minute and deduplicated to the latest result per target in that cycle.
A qualifying cycle requires at least the configured minimum number of transport-failing targets.
At least the configured fraction of observed targets in the cycle must have transport failures.
The same cycle must contain zero non-transport contract failures.
A timeout or a missing HTTP status with a non-empty error is a transport failure.
TLS-dominant cycles are reported separately when every transport failure in the qualifying cycle is a TCP/SSL handshake failure.
A later all-pass cycle can mark the latest qualifying event recovered without erasing recurrence history inside the lookback window.
invariants: The sentinel is observation-only and never mutates probe results, health observations, estate incidents, release admission or rollback state.
Raw estate state remains authoritative and is returned unchanged.
The sentinel never overrides the full-estate state.
A cycle containing any target-specific non-transport contract failure is excluded from shared-transport recurrence qualification.
Target-specific failures remain visible through raw estate and operational-attention evidence.
No automatic retry, application restart, evidence deletion, incident suppression or health-window mutation is authorised.
Browser roles receive no EXECUTE grant.
